title: Wall Painting of Monkeys in a Landscape
description: Blue monkeys navigating a rocky landscape; one of several related panels found together in the House of the Frescoes.

title: Captain of the Blacks
description: A red-skinned figure leading a file of dark-skinned soldiers; also known from an unrestored fragment version.

title: The Saffron-Gatherer
site: Knossos, Room of the Saffron Gatherer
description: Originally interpreted by Evans as a boy gathering saffron, now understood to depict a blue monkey; distinct from the similarly-named Akrotiri fresco.

title: Ladies in Blue
description: Three women in elaborate blue garments and jewelry; heavily restored from fragmentary evidence by Gillieron.

title: Griffins and Athletes
description: Mythic griffin figures paired with human athletes in a processional composition.

title: Grandstand / Sacred Grove and Dance
site: Knossos, north end of central court
description: Crowd scenes depicting spectators at a ritual gathering; among the most extensively reconstructed Knossos frescoes.

title: Goddess or Priestess from the Room of the Frescoes
site: Mycenae, Citadel House, Room of the Frescoes
description: A female figure positioned behind a household altar identified as a goddess or priestess; exact Commons file title needs manual verification.

title: Blue Monkeys Mural
description: Blue-painted monkeys climbing rocky terrain; subject of recent research proposing an Indus Valley (Indian langur) inspiration rather than African.

title: Young Man Carrying Fish (Fisherman Fresco)
period: Late Cycladic I / Late Minoan IA (c. 1650-1550 BCE)
description: A nude, partially shaved young man holds a cluster of fish in each hand tied with yellow string; likely depicts a religious ritual.

title: Boxing Boys
description: Two young boys wearing boxing gloves and belts, one of the best-known coming-of-age scenes from Akrotiri.

title: Wall Painting of a Procession of Women
description: Five women with right hands raised to their heads above another seven women each resting a hand on the shoulder of the woman ahead; found at a Minoan villa at Hagia Triada.

title: Wall Painting of Dolphins
description: Dolphins and fish swimming among rocky sea forms; one of the most reproduced Minoan images, though the ceiling placement of the original fragments is debated.
